bug.name: Nested jar URLs are parsed again on every cached resource lookup

description: Every lookup of a resource inside a nested jar builds and parses a java.net.URL, even when the nested JarFile is already cached.
JarUrlConnection.open needs a cache key, not a URL, but it builds the URL first and then derives the key from it.
It then builds a second key in cacheIfAbsent, which on a cache hit only proves the entry is already there.
Nothing is wrong in the output. The cost is allocation and time on a path a starting application walks thousands of times while probing for optional classes and package-info.
Measured on this machine: 480 bytes and 158 ns per warm-cache lookup that could be 192 bytes and 70 ns.

files.role: open(URL) builds `new URL(spec.substring(0, separator))` on line 340 before it ever consults the cache, and a second URL on line 342 for a runtime ref
getOrCreate -> Cache.get builds JarFileUrlKey number one; cacheIfAbsent -> Cache.putIfAbsent builds JarFileUrlKey number two, which is wasted on a hit
the key's only constructor takes a URL, which is why a URL has to exist before the cache can be read
the nested: handler that parseURL runs on every one of those URL constructions

repro.run: javac -d base $(find loader/spring-boot-loader/src/main/java -name '*.java' | grep -v '/launch/\|/jarmode/\|JarUrlClassLoader') && java -cp base -Xms512m -Xmx512m ...Repro
repro.expectation: Unpatched main at cf5f3b9e, three runs: 480 B/op at 157.8, 156.7 and 168.8 ns/op. With the fix below, same harness and same JVM: 192 B/op at 72.3, 70.0 and 75.2 ns/op. This is an allocation assertion, not a wall-clock one: 480 vs 192 bytes is exact and repeats to the byte, while the ns figures carry normal JIT noise.

why_bad: It is pure waste on a hot path: the URL that costs the allocation is thrown away as soon as the key is built, on every hit.
It scales with how hard a framework probes. Spring probes for optional classes and package-info across every nested jar at startup, so the cost lands where startup time is already scarce.
The reporter measured 1.03 GB of allocation on this path shrinking to 205 MB in a real application startup - garbage that the collector has to walk during the worst window for it.
Nothing surfaces it. Output is correct, no test fails, and the only symptom is allocation pressure that looks like the class loader being slow.
It is worse in memory-tight containers, where the extra garbage per lookup is what pushes a young collection during startup.

solution.summary: Build the cache key straight from the already-parsed nested spec and only construct a URL when the cache misses. One new package-private factory on JarFileUrlKey, one cache read on UrlJarFiles, and the URL work moved inside the miss branch of JarUrlConnection.open. No signature changes, no new fields, no behavior change on a miss.
notes: The constants in forNestedSpec are not guesses. Parsing nested:/tmp/app.jar/!BOOT-INF/lib/spring-core.jar through the registered handler yields protocol nested, host "", port -1, default port -1, and file equal to the spec with the nested: prefix removed, so the direct key is equal to the URL-derived one by JarFileUrlKey's own equals.
The miss branch is unchanged: same URL construction, same runtime ref handling, same getOrCreate and cacheIfAbsent, so cold behavior and concurrent misses keep the semantics they have today.
The second key in cacheIfAbsent disappears on a hit because cacheIfAbsent is no longer reached on a hit. It is untouched on a miss, where it is what makes the put atomic.

The file paths above are a shallow temp checkout of spring-projects/spring-boot at cf5f3b9e under $TMPDIR/bug-triage-src-spring-projects-spring-boot/; in the repo they are loader/spring-boot-loader/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/loader/net/protocol/jar/.
This is the reporter's own proposal. I did not invent an alternative; I implemented it in the temp clone to measure whether it removes the allocation it claims to remove.

files_to_touch.change: lines 340-346 - read the cache by direct key first, move the URL construction into the miss branch
add a private field constructor and the static forNestedSpec(spec, end, runtimeRef) factory
add getCached(JarFileUrlKey) and a Cache.get(JarFileUrlKey) overload that the URL overload delegates to
assert forNestedSpec equals and hashes the same as new JarFileUrlKey(url) for the same spec, with and without the runtime ref
cover a warm-cache nested lookup and a cold-cache miss so the two paths cannot drift apart

breaking.detail: No schema and no migration - the loader touches no database. All three classes are package-private inside org.springframework.boot.loader.net.protocol.jar, so nothing here is a published signature; the public JarUrl and the JarURLConnection contract are untouched. Callers see the same JarFile for the same URL, the same FileNotFoundException for a missing entry, and the same cache identity, because the new key is equal to the key that a URL would have produced. The one thing to keep honest is that equality: if the nested handler's parsing of protocol, host or port ever changes, the direct key and the URL key would drift, which is exactly what the JarFileUrlKeyTests addition is for.

safety.detail: The change is small, local, allocation-only, and reversible by a revert. I compiled unpatched main and the patched tree from the same sources and ran the same harness against both: 480 B/op before, 192 B/op after, with cold hit, warm hit and missing-entry behavior identical on both builds. The caveat is coverage, not design: my harness exercised cold, warm and missing on a synthetic two-entry nested jar. It did not exercise the runtime ref, a signed jar, a multi-release jar, or concurrent cold misses.
risks: forNestedSpec hard-codes what the nested handler produces today (protocol nested, host "", port -1). A change to that parsing would silently split the cache into two keys rather than fail loudly - a memory leak of duplicate JarFiles, not a wrong answer.

I could not exercise the runtime ref path: appending #runtime to a nested jar URL in my harness makes the loader look for a nested entry literally named nested.jar#runtime, and it fails that way on unpatched main too. That is a property of my synthetic fixture, not evidence about the fix, and it means the runtime ref branch is unmeasured here.
The measurement is one machine, one JVM (Corretto 25.0.2), one tiny nested jar. The direction matches the reporter's JMH numbers on a 168 MB jar; the absolute figures do not transfer.
I did not run Spring Boot's own test suite - no Gradle build was executed - so 'existing tests still pass' is not something this triage established.
verification: ./gradlew :loader:spring-boot-loader:test - the module's 551 loader tests, which this triage did not run.
Add the JarFileUrlKeyTests case asserting forNestedSpec(spec, end, runtimeRef) equals new JarFileUrlKey(new URL(spec)) for both ref states; that is the single assertion the whole change rests on.
Re-run the allocation harness on both builds and expect the exact byte figures to repeat: 480 B/op unpatched, 192 B/op patched.

For the end-to-end claim, take the reporter's route: JFR on a real application startup, and compare sample-weighted allocation on the JarUrlConnection.open path rather than wall-clock startup, which the reporter's own data could not resolve.
